name: Pwapwa

sources.citation: Rohleder, Jean. 2024. A grammar of Vamale (Language Science Press). [already held for vama1243]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §5.6 stress is for Vamale only (penultimate, weight-influenced); Pwapwâ appears only in pronoun/article comparison tables (from Leenhardt 1946 and 'Ozanne-Rivierre n.d.' unpublished Pwaamei/Pwapwâ dictionary) and in Ozanne-Rivierre's 1995 tree; no Pwapwâ stress statement.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 RA. 2012. Change Request 2012-129 [pop] (name Pwapwa -> Pwapwâ)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Rivierre, Jean-Claude. 'Langue de Voh-Koné' and 'Pwaamei' — fiches langue, DGLFLF Corpus de la parole (the Internet Archive 2011)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Voh-Koné fiche lists six dialects (Pwapwâ not among them), only phonological remark is *p,*ph > v,f.

sources.citation: Rivierre, Jean-Claude (LACITO). [2003/2008]. 'Pwapwâ' — fiche langue, DGLFLF 'Corpus de la parole' (text of the Les langues de France entry), Internet Archive copy 2011-08-29
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. States documentation = Leenhardt 1946 no.26 pp.144-149, Haudricourt 1963 survey, Ozanne-Rivierre surveys 1978 & 1981 with a Pwapwâ/Pwaamei publication 'in preparation'. 'Proche du pwaamei; langue conservatrice.'

sources.citation: Rivierre, Jean-Claude. 1978. Accents, tons et inversion tonale en Nouvelle-Calédonie. BSLP 73(1): 415-443 (archive.org djvu text, held under nemi1240)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes Xârâcùù initial (demarcative) accent and Paicî/Far-South tone; 'pwapwä' occurs only as no. 26 in the map legend; nothing on Pwapwâ or northern-group stress.

sources.citation: Rivierre, Jean-Claude. 1972. Les tons de la langue de Touho (cèmuhî). BSLP 67(1): 301-316 (archive.org djvu text, held under cemu1238)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Cèmuhî tonogenesis vs. 'dialectes sans tons de Voh-Koné et de la région de Hienghène'; '26- pwapwä' in map legend only; no stress-placement statement for Pwapwâ.

sources.citation: Haudricourt, André-Georges. 1961. Richesse en phonèmes et richesse en locuteurs. L'Homme 1(1): 5-10 (Persée)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Areal remarks on northern NC consonant richness; Voh/Koné spirants arose 'sous d'autres conditions prosodiques'; no statement of stress placement for any language.

sources.citation: Leenhardt, Maurice. 1946. Langues et dialectes de l'Austro-Mélanésie. Paris: Institut d'Ethnologie (Travaux et Mémoires 46). Chapter '26. — Poapoâ', pp. 144-149; general 'Phonétique' pp. 4-11; TOC pp. 675-676 (Gallica ark:/12148/bpt6k21694f, public domain, image-only; pages downloaded via IIIF and scanned with tesseract fra)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.144 has '§ 1. — Transcription' (consonant/vowel chart) followed by the heading '§ 2. — Accent et ton.' with NO text under it (blank questionnaire slot; same for Poamei p.150). General chapter p.11: 'Il reste à connaître l'accent, le ton.. On en trouvera le détail au chapitre réservé à chacune de celles-ci.' => silent on Pwapwâ stress.

sources.citation: Haudricourt, André-Georges. 1971. New Caledonia and the Loyalty Islands. In T. A. Sebeok (ed.), Current Trends in Linguistics, vol. 8: Linguistics in Oceania, 359-396. The Hague/Paris: Mouton.

sources.note: The only published linguistic overview that includes Haudricourt's own 1963 Pwapwâ (Boyen) data with per-language phoneme inventories; most likely place for a remark on accent in Pwapwâ/Pwaamei or the northern group generally.

sources.citation: Ozanne-Rivierre, Françoise. 1995. Structural changes in the languages of Northern New Caledonia. Oceanic Linguistics 34(1): 45-72.

sources.note: Classifies Pwapwâ with Pwaamei/Hienghène languages using her own data; possible prosodic remarks on the northern languages.

sources.citation: Rivierre, Jean-Claude. 1994. Contact-induced phonological complexification in New Caledonia. In T. Dutton & D. Tryon (eds.), Language Contact and Change in the Austronesian World, 497-522. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.

sources.note: Discusses prosody/aspirate development across the northern NC languages including the Voh–Hienghène area; may state the stress type of the non-tonal northern languages (second-hand/areal at best for Pwapwâ).

sources.citation: Ozanne-Rivierre, Françoise. 1992. The Proto-Oceanic consonantal system and the languages of New Caledonia. Oceanic Linguistics 31(2): 191-207.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: Uses her Pwapwâ field data (pp. 193-195, 201, 204-205 per OL index); the argument linking northern initial consonant strengthening to prosody may include an explicit statement on (initial) stress covering Pwapwâ.

sources.citation: Ozanne-Rivierre, Françoise. n.d. Dictionnaire thématique des langues pwaamei hnaakâ, pwaamei yaak et pwapwâ (Nouvelle-Calédonie). Unpublished manuscript (LACITO-CNRS; fieldwork 1978, 1981), cited in Rohleder 2024.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only modern first-hand description of Pwapwâ by a phonologist; her Hienghène dictionary (1982) has a phonological introduction, so this ms. very likely states the accent; would supersede everything else.
